normalisations: Request IDs are fixed: the 12 bytes of "vector-id-v1", then the exchange's number, big-endian, in the last 4 bytes. Database names are fixed (v001, v002, ...), one per exchange.

Values that differ from run to run (each listed in its vector's response.vary, a path with [] for every array element) are replaced inside the BSON by a fixed value of the same BSON type: a string by "normalised", an int32 or int64 by 1, a double by 1.0, a datetime by 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, a binary by the bytes of "normalised" with its subtype kept, an array by an empty array and a document by an empty document; the payload is then re-encoded. A driver checks a varying field's presence and BSON type, not its value.

Document field order: the server holds a stored document, and every document a request type declares as a map, as a Go map and encodes it in an unspecified order that differs from run to run. So the fields of every nested document in a request, and of every stored document in an answer (under data, doc, documents, results, value, element, metadata and values, and the document after a GET_FAST answer's status byte), are sorted by name. A driver compares documents field by field, never by their bytes.

Loopback ports the run happened to get are rewritten to fixed ones inside every string outside a stored document (the single node's driver port to 7433 and ring port to 4433; node1, node2 and node3 of the three-node cluster to driver ports 7433, 7434, 7435 and ring ports 4433, 4435, 4437; the not-yet-added node to 7436 and 4439), and the run's temporary directory to /data.
Server identities are fixed ed25519 keys made from fixed seeds, so fingerprints are the same in every run and are not normalised.

Fields that describe the capturing host rather than the protocol (health's capacity and memtable) are removed from the captured answer and listed in additive_fields: a driver must accept them and may not require them.

An ERROR answer written by the transport layer (its only fields are code and message) is encoded from a Go map, so its two fields arrive in either order; they are recorded sorted (code, then message).

vectors.name: alter bucket: refused in-band
vectors.notes: The request is database, name and replication_factor: a driver sends no other field. A factor the cluster cannot honour is an answer with success false and the message that says what to do, not an ERROR frame: the same request meets the same answer until an operator acts. No write_outcome is carried.

vectors.notes: The request is database, name and replication_factor: a driver sends no other field. node3 is stopped after the setup. The bucket is at three copies, its owner is node2 and node3 is the copy a decrease to two keeps; node3 cannot show it holds what node1's copy holds, so the owner refuses the decrease. The request goes to node1, which forwards it: the refusal is an ERROR frame UNAVAILABLE with write_outcome not_applied whichever node answers, because nothing changed and a retry is safe once node3 is back and has caught up. The refusals of an owner that clear by retrying (a placement pass still running, a copy still being made, a member that runs an older version) carry the same code and outcome.

payload_json.message: bucket not found: bucket "nobody" not found in database "v252". Run 'show buckets in v252' to list what exists, or 'create bucket nobody in v252 { type: hash }' to create it

vectors.name: alter bucket: missing bucket
vectors.notes: The request is database, name and replication_factor: a driver sends no other field. node3 is started again first if an earlier vector stopped it. No bucket of that name exists on any member, and its owner is node2 while the request goes to node1, which forwards it. The answer is an ERROR frame NOT_FOUND with write_outcome not_applied and the missing-bucket text every other verb gives, not UNAVAILABLE: no retry will make the bucket appear. It was UNAVAILABLE ("has no local copy"), the class a driver retries until its deadline.

payload_json.message: bucket not found: bucket "ghost001" not found in database "v253". Run 'show buckets in v253' to list what exists, or 'create bucket ghost001 in v253 { type: hash }' to create it

vectors.name: alter bucket: on a standalone node
vectors.notes: The request is database, name and replication_factor: a driver sends no other field. A standalone node has no cluster to place a second copy on, so it refuses an alter that raises the factor in the answer's own body: success false and the message that says to form a cluster, not an ERROR frame. The node's shape is judged before the bucket is looked up, so the answer is the same for a bucket that does not exist.

payload_json.message: bucket "users" cannot be raised to replication_factor 2: this server is running standalone, so there is no cluster to place a second copy on. Form a cluster as the replication page of the user docs describes, then run the alter once 'nodes' shows the members.

vectors.name: put to a bucket that does not exist, on a cluster
vectors.notes: node3 is started again first if an earlier vector stopped it. No bucket of that name exists on any member, and its owner is node2 while the request goes to node1, which forwards it. The answer is an ERROR frame NOT_FOUND with write_outcome not_applied and the same text a single node gives, not UNAVAILABLE: no retry will make the bucket appear, and UNAVAILABLE with not_applied is the class a driver retries until its deadline (BUG-0686).

payload_json.message: bucket not found: bucket "phantom001" not found in database "v255". Run 'show buckets in v255' to list what exists, or 'create bucket phantom001 in v255 { type: hash }' to create it

vectors.name: error with code 0
vectors.notes: Code 0 on an ERROR frame is INTERNAL, never success.

vectors.name: error with no code
vectors.notes: No code on an ERROR frame is INTERNAL, never success.

vectors.name: error with a code the driver does not know
vectors.notes: Kept as UNKNOWN(99) with the message, and treated like INTERNAL.

vectors.name: result too large with its two numbers
vectors.notes: max_result_bytes and retained_bytes (a lower bound) come only with RESULT_TOO_LARGE; the connection is unaffected. The live capture is the vector "a query over the result ceiling".

vectors.name: result too large with retained_bytes absent
vectors.notes: Captured live with HOARDDB_QUERY_MAX_RESULT_BYTES=1048576 over one document of 1.5 MB: the first result alone is over the ceiling, so nothing was retained and the server sends no retained_bytes (it does not send a zero), which a driver reads as 0. max_result_bytes is present, and the connection is unaffected.

vectors.name: batch over the store's atomic bound
vectors.notes: BATCH_TOO_LARGE with write_outcome not_applied: nothing of the batch was written; halve it and resend. A driver splits on the code and never on the message. Built with the server's own message (server/errors.go:OverBoundBatchMessage) because the live request is about 5 MB, which the file's size budget leaves to harness leg 6.

vectors.name: write concern not met in time
vectors.notes: TIMEOUT with write_outcome applied: the write is stored; never resend it. Message format of server/write_path.go:concernNotMet.

vectors.name: unavailable with an unknown write outcome
vectors.notes: The owner changed under the write: write_outcome unknown, so the caller reads back before resending. Message format of server/write_path.go:ownershipMovedErr.

vectors.name: auth refused with an empty payload
vectors.notes: An empty AUTH_FAIL, which older servers send, is CREDENTIALS.

vectors.name: auth refused: tokens unsupported
vectors.notes: Reason 4: a server without the auth_token capability. This server never sends it; a driver discards its tokens.

vectors.name: auth refused: internal
vectors.notes: Reason 8: here, a cluster node that has not received its user configuration. Not a credential failure; retry on another node or after a short wait. Message of server/authconfig.go:Server.authConfigUnavailableReason.

vectors.name: delete answered skipped
vectors.notes: a conditional delete (expire_if) of an expired document whose store fields hold more elements than one atomic batch deletes answers success false and skipped true, and leaves the document whole. Provoking it takes about 125,000 store-field elements, so it is built with the server's own DeleteResponse; the message follows server/fieldstore.go:expirySkippedMessage. The live delete vectors with expire_if (expired, and spared) are exchanges.

payload_json.message: Document "s1" in bucket "sessions" of database "v000" has expired and was not deleted: its store fields hold too many elements to delete in one step (Events: 125,000). It is left whole and every TTL sweep tries it again. Empty its store fields — db.sessions["s1"].Events.pop() until len() is 0 — and the next sweep expires it, or delete the document yourself once they are empty.

vectors.name: error frame with a zero request ID and no payload fields
vectors.notes: A refusal is read as the answer to whatever was in flight.

vectors.name: connection refused: no ALPN offered
vectors.notes: Captured live: a client that offers no ALPN completes TLS and receives this, then the connection closes.

vectors.name: connection refused: overloaded
vectors.notes: Captured live with HOARDDB_TCP_MAX_CONNS_PER_IP=1 and one connection held: the refusal carries a zero request ID and the connection closes. Not fatal to a pool: back off that one dial.

vectors.name: an oversize request is answered by its request ID
vectors.notes: Captured live: request_header_hex is a BATCH_PUT header whose length word is 96 MiB, sent before AUTH with no body. The server answers INVALID_ARGUMENT echoing the request ID, naming the size, the 32 MiB limit and the remedy, then closes (before AUTH, or over 64 MiB). A driver refuses such a frame itself, before writing it.

vectors.name: fingerprint of key 1
vectors.notes: SHA256: and the lowercase hex of SHA-256 over the raw 32-byte ed25519 public key (the last 32 bytes of the certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo), from the key and from the certificate alike.

vectors.name: fingerprint of key 2
vectors.notes: SHA256: and the lowercase hex of SHA-256 over the raw 32-byte ed25519 public key (the last 32 bytes of the certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo), from the key and from the certificate alike.
